topics.why_now: The Eclipse Foundation launched a multi-organization Sovereign AI Foundation to map dependencies, evaluate open alternatives and develop guidance across models, tooling and agentic systems.
topics.practical_value: Provides a framework for teams evaluating dependency risk, portability, governance and local control across the AI stack.
topics.limitations: The foundation is newly launched; concrete reference architectures, adoption evidence and interoperability outcomes are still emerging.
topics.next_action: Track the foundation’s dependency maps, reference architectures and concrete cross-stack interoperability guidance.

topics.name: Full-duplex human interaction models
topics.audience: Multimodal AI builders, product teams, and interaction designers
topics.summary: Unified real-time models listen, watch and respond concurrently instead of chaining separate turn-based components.
topics.why_now: Tavus introduced Griffin-Lite as a unified real-time video-to-video system that listens, watches and responds concurrently, shifting multimodal interfaces from turn-taking pipelines toward continuous interaction while explicitly retaining release-safety limits.
topics.practical_value: Could make video agents respond to speech, expression and visual context continuously rather than waiting for discrete turns.
topics.limitations: The reviewed evidence is an early vendor research preview with explicit release-safety limits; independent latency, quality and safety evaluation is still needed.
topics.next_action: Track public access, independent real-time interaction tests, safety controls and performance under interruption and noisy visual scenes.

topics.name: Open agent hardware moves from demos to kits
topics.audience: Agent builders, hardware experimenters, and open-source communities
topics.summary: Open code and commodity boards are turning personal-agent gadgets into reproducible community hardware projects.
topics.why_now: Meta's newly open-sourced Muse gadget code targets ESP32 and Raspberry Pi builds, suggesting personal agents may become a community hardware layer rather than remain confined to phones and desktops.
topics.practical_value: Could let teams prototype ambient or dedicated agents on auditable, replaceable hardware outside phone and desktop ecosystems.
topics.limitations: The current signal is open-source gadget code and reporting, not evidence of a mature, secure or broadly supported hardware platform.
topics.next_action: Inspect the released code, bill of materials, permission model, update path and independent builds on ESP32 and Raspberry Pi hardware.
